about.pl: Rubryki nazywają zdanie poprzedzające Pater noster prefacją Modlitwy Pańskiej. Po słowach et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem odpowiedź sed líbera nos a malo przypisują ministrantowi. We Mszy czytanej wierni mogą odmówić całe Ojcze nasz razem z kapłanem, po łacinie, i dodać z nim Amen.
about.en: The rubrics call the sentence before Pater noster the preface of the Lord's Prayer. After et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, they assign the response sed líbera nos a malo to the server. At low Mass the faithful may say the whole Our Father with the priest, in Latin, and add the Amen with him.

function.pl: Następujący embolizm rozpoczyna ten sam tryb rozkazujący: Líbera nos, quǽsumus, Dómine.
function.en: The embolism that follows begins with the same imperative: Líbera nos, quǽsumus, Dómine.

function.pl: Dopełnienie líbera w bierniku.
function.en: Accusative object of líbera.

function.pl: Wydanie analizuje „malo” jako rzeczownik nijaki oznaczający zło. Następujący embolizm podejmuje je w liczbie mnogiej: „ab ómnibus malis”. Katechizm wyjaśnia zarazem, że prośba odnosi się ostatecznie do Złego (KKK 2851).
function.en: This edition parses “malo” as the neuter noun for evil. The following embolism takes it up in the neuter plural, “ab ómnibus malis.” The Catechism also explains that the petition ultimately refers to the Evil One (CCC 2851).

note.pl: Forma jest ablatiwem obu słów naraz. Może to być malum — zło, rzecz zła — albo malus — Zły, czyli szatan. Ani forma, ani zdanie nie rozstrzygają, i tradycja czyta to na oba sposoby. Ta edycja przyjmuje malum i zaznacza wątpliwość.
note.en: The form is the ablative of both words at once. It can be malum, evil as a thing, or malus, the Evil One. Neither the form nor the sentence decides, and the tradition reads it both ways. This edition takes malum and marks the doubt.

function.pl: To Amen wypowiada kapłan.
function.en: This Amen is said by the priest.

editorial.notes: The Lord's Prayer as the Mass sets it: the preface Orémus. Præcéptis salutáribus móniti, the prayer said by the priest alone as far as tentatiónem, the server's Sed líbera nos a malo, and the priest's Amen — the Ordo's page rubric says secrete, the Ritus servandus (X, 1) submissa voce; the edition follows the page rubric and records the disagreement for the expert. The words of the prayer are RE-ENCODED here rather than referenced. The corpus already carries orationes.pater-noster, the same prayer in its devotional form, and the letters are identical; but that document is one continuous text said by one voice, while this one is a dialogue — the last petition belongs to another speaker — wrapped in a preface and divided by three rubrics. Those are two recensions of one prayer, which is what the variant field is for, and the corpus already keeps recension pairs apart with their own word ids (ordinarium.confiteor and ordinarium.confiteor-sacerdotis, ordinarium.misereatur and ordinarium.misereatur-tui — those pairs differ in wording; this pair alone is letter-identical). The schema has no field by which one text could borrow another's words, and a reference would leave a hole in the middle of a prayer the reader is praying. MÓNITI at w004 and FORMÁTI at w008 are participles, not adjectives: neither analyzer heads an adjective monitus or formatus, only the verbs and nouns of their own (monitus, -us — a reminding) that are not the adjective claimed. AUDÉMUS at w009 is present indicative; audeo is semi-deponent, so only its perfect system is deponent in form. NE at w050 is the prohibitive adverb, as the corpus rules it elsewhere.
